1: # Open CVN
2: 
3: ## Descripcion
4: 
5: Este repositorio contiene un Trabajo de Fin de Grado orientado a definir un
6: esquema de datos abierto para la representacion de curriculos en el ambito
7: universitario y de investigacion en Espana, tomando como punto de partida el
8: formato CVN.
9: 
10: El problema de partida es que, aunque el CVN existe como formato normalizado,
11: la elaboracion, mantenimiento y adaptacion de curriculos a distintos contextos
12: sigue consumiendo mucho tiempo y dificulta el desarrollo de herramientas
13: abiertas interoperables. Una de las causas es la ausencia de una definicion de
14: bajo nivel suficientemente clara para representar y procesar estos datos.
15: 
16: ## Objetivo Del Proyecto
17: 
18: El objetivo general del TFG es definir un esquema de datos que permita la
19: gestion automatizada de curriculos academicos y de investigacion en Espana.
20: 
21: Ese objetivo se descompone en varias lineas de trabajo:
22: 
23: 1. estudiar el formato CVN actual y analizar sus limitaciones
24: 2. proponer un formato de bajo nivel agnostico respecto al formato final de
25:    representacion
26: 3. definir un esquema final basado en JSON, apto para ficheros de texto y bases
27:    de datos NoSQL
28: 4. desarrollar una aplicacion en Python para lectura y validacion de curriculos
29:    utilizando Pydantic
30: 5. desarrollar herramientas de almacenamiento local y exportacion a LaTeX
31: 6. explorar el uso de LLM para importar curriculos generados por herramientas
32:    externas como la aplicacion de la FECYT
33: 
34: ## Alcance Actual Del Repositorio
35: 
36: La infraestructura que actualmente se esta construyendo para generar modelos
37: Pydantic es solo una parte del proyecto total. En esta fase, el foco del
38: repositorio esta en sentar la base tecnica del pipeline que permitira:
39: 
40: 1. traducir los artefactos oficiales CVN XML/XSD a bindings estructurales
41:    Pydantic
42: 2. normalizar la metadata funcional y tecnica del paquete oficial
43: 3. generar mas adelante modelos de dominio reutilizables y un esquema final mas
44:    limpio
45: 
46: Esta base es necesaria para el parser/validador en Python, pero no agota el TFG:
47: todavia quedan por delante la definicion del modelo final, la capa JSON, la
48: exportacion a LaTeX, y la futura exploracion de una herramienta de importacion
49: basada en LLM.
50: 
51: ## Direccion Tecnica Actual
52: 
53: El repositorio sigue una arquitectura de dos capas:
54: 
55: 1. bindings estructurales generados a partir del paquete oficial CVN
56: 2. modelos semanticos y de dominio que se generaran sobre metadata normalizada
57: 
58: La arquitectura, el estado actual y el roadmap se documentan en el propio
59: repositorio para que futuras sesiones no dependan de reconstruir el contexto a
60: partir del chat o de issues externos.
61: 
62: ## Punto De Entrada
63: 
64: Para obtener el contexto del proyecto y el estado real de implementacion, leer:
65: 
66: 1. `PROJECT_GUIDE.md`
67: 2. `docs/context/project_context_index.md`
68: 3. `docs/context/current_status.md`
69: 
70: ## Documentos Clave
71: 
72: - guia principal del proyecto:
73:   `PROJECT_GUIDE.md`
74: - indice de contexto del proyecto:
75:   `docs/context/project_context_index.md`
76: - estado actual del proyecto:
77:   `docs/context/current_status.md`
78: - arquitectura del pipeline:
79:   `docs/pipeline/cvn_pydantic_generation_pipeline.md`
80: - roadmap completo:
81:   `docs/roadmap/cvn_generation_roadmap.md`
82: - guia de contribucion y setup:
83:   `CONTRIBUTING.md`
84: 

(End of file - total 84 lines)

1: # Hotfix 3 - CVN Source Package Documentation Expansion
2: 
3: ## Summary
4: 
5: This maintenance record documents the documentation-only patch applied during the
6: session that expanded repository coverage of the canonical CVN source package.
7: 
8: ## Motivation
9: 
10: The repository already documented the core CVN structural artifacts, but the
11: canonical source bundle also included several auxiliary families and a large set
12: of Annex I tables that were not documented in equivalent depth.
13: 
14: That gap made later semantic work harder because future sessions would still need
15: to reopen the original package to understand:
16: 
17: - how side-package artifacts related to core CVN files
18: - which Annex I tables were technically represented
19: - which references were subtype-backed, hierarchical, or unresolved
20: - how current normalization output should be interpreted without changing the
21:   existing core
22: 
23: ## Scope Of This Patch
24: 
25: This patch is documentation-only.
26: 
27: It does not change:
28: 
29: - structural bindings
30: - normalization contracts from issue `#13`
31: - tests or runtime code
32: 
33: It adds and updates persistent documentation so the repository can be resumed
34: without reconstructing source-package semantics from chat history.
35: 
36: ## Documentation Added
37: 
38: The following persistent documents were added:
39: 
40: - `docs/cvn_source_package_auxiliary_artifacts.md`
41: - `docs/cvn_source_package_annex_table_coverage.md`
42: - `docs/cvn_annex_priority_table_families.md`
43: - `docs/cvn_annex_table_families_batch3.md`
44: - `docs/cvn_annex_table_families_batch4.md`
45: - `docs/cvn_annex_table_families_batch5.md`
46: - `docs/cvn_annex_table_families_batch6.md`
47: - `docs/cvn_annex_table_families_batch7.md`
48: - `docs/cvn_annex_table_families_batch8.md`
49: - `docs/cvn_serialization_patterns_reference.md`
50: - `docs/cvn_field_reference_traceability.md`
51: 
52: ## Documentation Updated
53: 
54: The following repository entry or context documents were updated to point to the
55: new reference material and to keep the global context aligned:
56: 
57: - `PROJECT_GUIDE.md`
58: - `docs/context/project_context_index.md`
59: - `docs/context/current_status.md`
60: - `docs/pipeline/cvn_pydantic_generation_pipeline.md`
61: - `docs/pipeline/known_limitations.md`
62: - `docs/informe_estructura_cvnxml_v1.4.3.md`
63: - `docs/roadmap/issues/issue-14-semantic-mapping-rules.md`
64: 
65: ## Main Outcomes
66: 
67: This patch established the following persistent knowledge in the repository.
68: 
69: ### 1. Side-Package Families Are Now Explicitly Documented
70: 
71: The repository now documents the structure, role, and relationships of:
72: 
73: - `Entity`
74: - `ReferenceTables/Subtypes`
75: - `Thesaurus`
76: 
77: ### 2. Annex I Coverage Is Now Explicitly Classified
78: 
79: The repository now distinguishes between:
80: 
81: - tables represented directly in core XSD artifacts
82: - tables represented through side-package XML/XSD artifacts
83: - manual-only or unresolved references
84: 
85: ### 3. Detailed Coverage Of `ReferenceTables.xml` Is Complete
86: 
87: All tables present in `ReferenceTables.xml` are now documented explicitly in the
88: repository, including:
89: 
90: - high-priority families such as `CVN_SOURCE_*`, `CVN_TITLE_*`, `CVN_PROJECT_*`,
91:   `CVN_ENTITY_TYPE`, and `UNESCO_CODES`
92: - subsequent batches covering participation, programmes, publications, support,
93:   events, activities, management, scope, language, time, qualification, access,
94:   subject, stays, dedication, prizes, thematic tables, geography, situation,
95:   agencies, collaboration, supervision, categories, and residual tables
96: 
97: ### 4. Special Cases Are Now Explicitly Recorded
98: 
99: The repository now preserves the following cases as explicit documentation facts:
100: 
101: - `CVN_AGENCY_C` is referenced by the manual but does not have a clean matching
102:   table in `ReferenceTables.xml`
103: - `CVN_INTERVENTION_A` and `CVN_PRUEBA` exist in `ReferenceTables.xml` but do not
104:   currently show a clear use site in `SpecificationManual.xml`
105: - `CVN_KNOW_A` is a subtype-backed industrial-property table and must be treated
106:   as such in later semantic work
107: 
108: ### 5. Serialization Patterns Are Now Documented Separately From The Core
109: 
110: The repository now records the main serialization patterns used by CVN tables,
111: including:
112: 
113: - `Filter/Value`
114: - `Quality/Measure`
115: - `Scope/Type`
116: - `ExternalPK/Type`
117: - `Entity/Type`
118: - `Dedication`
119: - `PhysicalDimension/Type`
120: - `Subject/Description`
121: - `Subtype@Subtypes.xsd`
122: - side-package catalog patterns
123: - unresolved manual-only references
124: 
125: ### 6. Existing Normalization Output Now Has An Operational Interpretation Guide
126: 
127: The repository now documents how to interpret the already implemented
128: `ManualCodeEntry.manual_reference_table` field from issue `#13` without changing
129: the normalization core.
130: 
131: ## Consistency Cleanup Performed
132: 
133: During the same session, documentation consistency issues were also corrected:
134: 
135: - outdated project snapshot in `project_context_index.md`
136: - outdated wording around issue `#13`
137: - missing issue `#25` mention in `PROJECT_GUIDE.md`
138: - incomplete implemented-issues list in `project_context_index.md`
139: - ambiguous reading-order wording in `current_status.md`
140: - missing cross-links between Annex coverage, serialization patterns, and field
141:   traceability documents
142: - mismatch between traceability examples and named serialization patterns
143: - excessive repetition in the status summary was compressed to a more stable form
144: 
145: ## Impact On Later Issues
146: 
147: This patch does not implement issue `#14`, but it substantially reduces semantic
148: discovery work for it.
149: 
150: The new documentation should make it easier to:
151: 
152: - define semantic mapping rules without re-reading the whole source package
153: - classify table references correctly by technical pattern
154: - distinguish compact enums from hierarchical codelists and large registries
155: - keep future work compatible with the current normalization core
156: 
157: ## Status
158: 
159: - Status: completed

(End of file - total 159 lines)
</content>

1: # Project Guide
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This file is the human entry point for understanding the repository.
6: It summarizes the project purpose, the current implementation focus, the
7: documentation structure, and the repository rules that matter to contributors
8: and maintainers.
9: 
10: ## What This Repository Is
11: 
12: This repository contains a Trabajo de Fin de Grado focused on defining an open
13: data schema for representing academic and research CVs in Spain, taking the
14: CVN format as the starting point.
15: 
16: The long-term goal is not only to mirror the official CVN package, but to make
17: curriculum data easier to validate, transform, store, and export through open
18: tooling.
19: 
20: ## Current Technical Scope
21: 
22: The repository is currently centered on the generation pipeline that turns the
23: official CVN XML/XSD package into reproducible Python artifacts.
24: 
25: Current and planned layers are:
26: 
27: 1. structural bindings generated from the official CVN XML/XSD package
28: 2. normalized metadata extracted from the official supporting XML documents
29: 3. semantic mapping rules that recover domain meaning from the structural layer
30: 4. domain-oriented Pydantic models built over normalized metadata
31: 
32: This means the repository is currently implementing the technical foundation
33: for the future parser, validator, JSON-oriented schema, and downstream export
34: work. It is not yet the full end-user CV tooling envisioned by the TFG.
35: 
36: ## Recommended Reading Order For Humans
37: 
38: When you need to understand the project state before making changes, read these
39: files in order:
40: 
41: 1. `PROJECT_GUIDE.md`
42: 2. `docs/context/project_context_index.md`
43: 3. `docs/context/current_status.md`
44: 4. the relevant issue document under `docs/roadmap/issues/`
45: 5. supporting architecture or limitation documents linked from that issue
46: 
47: ## Repository Rules And Conventions
48: 
49: - Treat `docs/CvnXML_v1.4.3_2.1_17012025/` as the canonical source package for

This repository contains a Trabajo de Fin de Grado focused on defining an open
data schema for representing academic and research CVs in Spain, taking the
CVN format as the starting point.

curriculum data easier to validate, transform, store, and export through open
tooling.

1: # Issue 11 - Project Infrastructure For Code Generation
2: 
3: ## Summary
4: 
5: Issue `#11` established the repository baseline required for the CVN generation
6: pipeline. It did not generate final bindings or domain models. Its role was to
7: fix the repository structure, generation tooling, and structural generation
8: policy so later issues could build on a stable foundation.
9: 
10: ## Original Goal
11: 
12: - prepare the project infrastructure for reproducible code generation
13: - define the repository layout for generated code, manual pipeline logic, and
14:   future domain models
15: - standardize the use of `xsdata` and `xsdata-pydantic`
16: 
17: ## Original Plan
18: 
19: 1. adopt a `src/` layout
20: 2. reserve `src/generated/` for generated structural bindings
21: 3. reserve `src/cvn_codegen/` for hand-maintained pipeline logic
22: 4. reserve `src/models/cvn/` for domain-facing models
23: 5. define code generation dependencies separately from runtime dependencies
24: 6. add a shared `xsdata` configuration file under `config/.xsdata.xml`
25: 7. treat the structural layer as a faithful interoperability layer rather than
26:    the final domain model
27: 
28: ## Adjustments Made During Implementation
29: 
30: The original infrastructure plan proved directionally correct, but by the time
31: issue `#12` started two operational adjustments were needed to make the
32: baseline fully usable:
33: 
34: 1. `src/models/cvn/` had to be created explicitly to match the planned layout
35: 2. editable packaging support was added so the `src/` layout would be importable
36:    during tests and local execution
37: 
38: These adjustments did not change the conceptual architecture of `#11`; they
39: made the baseline operational.
40: 
41: ## Implementation Performed
42: 
43: ### Repository Layout
44: 
45: The baseline layout established by issue `#11` is:
46: 
47: ```text
48: src/
49: ├── generated/
50: │   ├── cvn/
51: │   ├── specification_manual/
52: │   └── tree_model/
53: ├── cvn_codegen/
54: └── models/
55:     └── cvn/
56: ```
57: 
58: ### Tooling Baseline
59: 
60: - dependency management: `uv`
61: - structural generation tooling: `xsdata[cli,lxml]`
62: - Pydantic binding support: `xsdata-pydantic`
63: - structural generation config: `config/.xsdata.xml`
64: 
65: ### Packaging Baseline
66: 
67: To support the `src/` layout in practice, the repository now also has:
68: 
69: - a `setuptools` build backend in `pyproject.toml`
70: - editable installation support for local development
71: - `src/cvn_codegen/__init__.py` so the package is importable during tests and
72:   runner execution
73: 
74: ## Verification
75: 
76: The infrastructure was validated by successfully using it in issue `#12` to:
77: 
78: - generate structural bindings under `src/generated/`
79: - import the runner from `cvn_codegen`
80: - run `pytest` against the runner tests
81: 
82: ## Findings
83: 
84: - The original architectural decisions from issue `#11` were sufficient and did
85:   not require redesign
86: - The `src/` layout benefits from explicit packaging support when tests and
87:   module execution start relying on it
88: 
89: ## Known Limitations
90: 
91: - Issue `#11` intentionally did not solve semantic modeling concerns
92: - It also did not define the full regeneration workflow end-to-end; that work
93:   continues through issues `#12` to `#17`
94: 
95: ## Impact On Future Issues
96: 
97: - Issue `#12` reuses the exact structural package layout defined here
98: - Issues `#13` to `#15` depend on the separation between generated artifacts and
99:   manual pipeline logic
100: - Issue `#17` will document the workflow, but it is grounded in the structure
101:   introduced here
102: 
103: ## Status
104: 
105: - Status: completed and validated as the operational baseline for the CVN
106:   generation roadmap

(End of file - total 106 lines)
</content>

2:

7: smoke tests for the generation workflow.

14:   - `CVNTreeModel_v1.0.xsd`

21: 2. generate `SpecificationManual.xsd` bindings under
22:    `src/generated/specification_manual/`
23: 3. generate `CVNTreeModel_v1.0.xsd` bindings under
24:    `src/generated/tree_model/`
25: 4. verify local `include` and `import` resolution
26: 5. verify generated modules can be imported
27: 6. test at least one parse flow for `SpecificationManual.xml`
28: 7. test at least one parse flow for `CVNTreeModel.xml`
29: 8. record structural limitations and generation friction
30: 
31: ## Adjustments Made During Implementation
32: 
33: The original plan was refined in several ways during execution:
34: 
35: 1. a standardized runner was created before generation to make execution
36:    reproducible and testable
37: 2. smoke tests were added as part of issue `#12` instead of waiting entirely
38:    for issue `#16`
39: 3. editable packaging support was added so tests could import `cvn_codegen` and
40:    `generated.*` cleanly from the `src/` layout
41: 4. generation had to be executed with `cwd=src` so package names such as
42:    `generated.cvn` mapped to `src/generated/cvn`
43: 5. `tree_model` required a target-specific xsdata override (`--unnest-classes`)
44:    to avoid generation failure from circular dependencies
45: 6. the parse goal for `CVNTreeModel.xml` was partially blocked by a mismatch
46:    between the canonical XML and its XSD, which had to be documented as a
47:    limitation instead of being silently patched in the structural layer
48: 
49: ## Implementation Performed
50: 
51: ### Standardized Runner
52: 
53: The following runner was introduced:
54: 
55: - `src/cvn_codegen/xsdata_runner.py`
56: 
57: Responsibilities implemented:
58: 
59: - resolve supported targets (`cvn`, `specification_manual`, `tree_model`,
60:   `all`)
61: - validate prerequisites
62: - clean the destination package before generation
63: - build deterministic xsdata commands
64: - execute generation from `src/`
65: - verify generated output
66: 
67: ### Generated Structural Packages
68: 
69: Bindings were generated under:
70: 
71: - `src/generated/cvn/`
72: - `src/generated/specification_manual/`
73: - `src/generated/tree_model/`

78: 
79: - `tests/test_xsdata_runner_unit.py`
80: - `tests/test_xsdata_runner_smoke.py`
81: 
82: ## Verification
83: 
84: ### Generation
85: 
86: Generation was successfully executed for:
87: 
88: - `CVN.xsd`
89: - `SpecificationManual.xsd`
90: - `CVNTreeModel_v1.0.xsd`
91: 
92: ### Import Checks
93: 
94: The generated packages are importable:
95: 
96: - `generated`
97: - `generated.cvn`
98: - `generated.specification_manual`
99: - `generated.tree_model`
100: 
101: ### Parse Smoke Checks
102: 
103: #### `SpecificationManual.xml`
104: 
105: - Result: success
106: - Parser: `xsdata_pydantic.bindings.XmlParser`
107: - Root class: `generated.specification_manual.SpecificationManual`
108: 
109: #### `CVNTreeModel.xml`
110: 
111: - Result: failure
112: - Root class: `generated.tree_model.CvntreeModel`
113: - Cause: the canonical XML contains `<Type>` inside `Indicator`, but

115: 
116: ## Findings
117: 
118: ### Positive Results
119: 
120: - Structural bindings for all three source concerns can be generated
121: - Generated packages under `src/generated/` are importable
122: - The runner standardizes generation successfully
123: - `SpecificationManual.xml` can be parsed with the generated binding

310: ## Agreed `xml_path` Convention
311: 
312: ### Purpose
313: 
314: - `xml_path` is the normalized structural path used to identify where a code is
315:   modeled inside `CVNTreeModel.xml`
316: - it is meant for traceability, grouping, and later semantic processing
317: - it is not intended to duplicate the semantic content already carried by
318:   `code`, `tree_value`, or manual metadata fields
319: 
320: ### Structural Scope
321: 
322: - `xml_path` is an absolute structural path rooted at `CVNTreeModel`
323: - it is built only from the standard structural nodes of the documented tree
324:   model:
325:   - `CVNTreeModel`
326:   - `Node`
327:   - `Version`
328:   - `Agent`
329:   - `CVNItem`
330:   - `Property`
331:   - `Indicator`

333: ### Segment Rules
334: 
335: - the root must always begin with:
336:   - `/CVNTreeModel/Node`
337: - `Version` and `Agent` are represented by their literal node names:
338:   - `/CVNTreeModel/Node/Version/...`
339:   - `/CVNTreeModel/Node/Agent/...`
340: - `CVNItem` is represented with its `code` when available:
341:   - `CVNItem[@code='010.010.000.000']`
342: - `Property` is represented with its technical `name` when available:
343:   - `Property[@name='Identification']`
344: - `Indicator` is represented with its technical `name` when available:
345:   - `Indicator[@name='Gender']`
346: - when `name` is missing, the segment falls back to the plain node name:
347:   - `Property`
348:   - `Indicator`

352: - `Value` is not part of `xml_path`
353: - the `code` of `Property` is not part of `xml_path`
354: - the `code` of `Indicator` is not part of `xml_path`
355: - default-value semantics are not part of `xml_path`
356: - unexpected source nodes that are not part of the documented structural model
357:   are not part of `xml_path`
358: 
359: ### Examples
360: 
361: - example path for a direct agent field:
362:   - `/CVNTreeModel/Node/Agent/Property[@name='Identification']/Indicator[@name='PersonalIdentification']/Indicator[@name='Gender']`
363: - example path for a CVN item field:
364:   - `/CVNTreeModel/Node/CVNItem[@code='010.010.000.000']/Property[@name='Title']/Indicator[@name='Name']`
365: - when an indicator carries a `Value`, that value is stored in `tree_value`, not
366:   appended to the path
367:

369: 
370: ### Validation Against `TreeModel_v1.0 20090331 v1.0.pdf`
371: 
372: - the document defines the official structural model using:
373:   - `CVNTreeModel`
374:   - `Node`

377:   - `CVNItem`
378:   - `Property`

383: - for `Indicator`, the document identifies:
384:   - `name`
385:   - `code`
386:   - `Value`
387:   - `Child`

389:   - `@code` only for `CVNItem`
390:   - `@name` for `Property`
391:   - `@name` for `Indicator`
392:   - no `Value` in the path itself

394: ### Validation Against The Technical Specification Manual

398:   - code
399:   - short name

403:   - multiplicity and linkage
404: - this confirms that `xml_path` should remain a structural locator, while the
405:   semantic meaning of each field continues to come from `SpecificationManual.xml`

407: ## Confirmed Tree-Model Source Inconsistency Relevant To `xml_path`
408: 
409: - the canonical `CVNTreeModel.xml` contains `438` `Indicator` nodes with
410:   `mo:name="Type"`, which is structurally normal

414:   - `Indicator mo:name="Type" mo:code="060.030.070.220"`
415:   - `Indicator mo:name="Type" mo:code="060.030.070.230"`
416: - both unexpected child elements contain:
417:   - `CVN_QualityTypeType@AuxTable.xsd`
418: - `TreeModel_v1.0 20090331 v1.0.pdf` documents `Indicator` children as only:
419:   - `Value`
420:   - `Child`
421: - this means the two `<Type>` elements behave as source inconsistencies, not as
422:   a documented feature of the tree model
423: - as a consequence, those nodes must be treated as mismatches or special-case
424:   findings during normalization, not as part of the standard `xml_path` model

1: # Issue 14 - Define Semantic Mapping Rules And Override Policy
2: 
3: ## Summary
4: 
5: Issue `#14` will define the rules that transform normalized CVN metadata into
6:  domain-oriented Pydantic models.

8: ## Original Goal

143:   - a wrapper-based field such as date or duration
144:   - a case that requires an explicit override
145: - goal: ensure issue `#15` can consume the policy without reopening semantic
146:   design questions already settled here
147: 
148: ### Step `10` - Document The Final Policy And Unresolved Limits
149: 
150: - record final decisions in versioned repository documentation
151: - document any semantic ambiguities that remain unresolved after issue `#14`
152: - if a new limitation is discovered, record it in
153:   `docs/pipeline/known_limitations.md`
154: - if issue state changes, update the roadmap and current status documents in the
155:   same session
156: 
157: ## Questions Still To Decide
158: 
159: Before issue `#14` can be considered fully specified, some semantic decisions
160: still need to be made explicitly:
161: 
162: 1. whether future domain-facing names should prefer Spanish academic
163:    terminology, English conceptual terminology, or a documented hybrid rule
164: 2. which categories of controlled tables should become strict enums and which
165:    should remain open representations
166: 3. how external reference tables such as `ENTITY@Entity.xsd`,
167:    `THESAURUS@thesaurus.xsd`, and `UNESCO_CODES` should be represented in the
168:    semantic layer
169: 4. whether wrappers like flexible dates and durations should become primitives,
170:    unions, or dedicated value objects in the future domain API
171: 5. what exact shape the override registry should take so later generation stays
172:    deterministic and reviewable
173: 
174: ## Minimum Decisions Required
175: 
176: 1. which wrappers collapse to primitives in the domain layer
177: 2. which controlled sets become enums and which remain strings
178: 3. how multilingual names affect class and field naming
179: 4. how multiplicity becomes optional fields versus `list[T]`
180: 5. how external reference tables remain represented
181: 6. how code-specific exceptions are registered outside the generic algorithm
182: 
183: ## Constraints To Respect
184: 
185: - many structural XSD types are technical wrappers rather than domain concepts
186: - some reference tables are internal and some are external to the package
187: - `choice` appears rarely but in high-value structures
188: - XML interoperability metadata should not leak into the future domain API by
189:   default
190: 
191: ## Relevant Known Inputs
192: 
193: - structural bindings preserve fidelity but expose known limitations for
194:   `choice`, multiplicity, and wrapper ergonomics
195: - the official source package does include side-package material for several
196:   references previously treated as opaque placeholders:
197:   - `ENTITY@Entity.xsd` is represented by the `Entity` family
198:   - `THESAURUS@thesaurus.xsd` is represented by the `Thesaurus` family
199:   - many Annex-I tables are materialized in `ReferenceTables.xml`
200: - not all manual references are fully resolved from the package alone; a known
201:   example is `CVN_AGENCY_C`
202: 
203: ## Status
204: 
205: - Status: pending

1: # Issue 25 - GitHub Actions CI Pipeline For PR Testing On Main And Development
2: 
3: ## Summary
4: 
5: Issue `#25` adds a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the repository test suite
6: for pull requests targeting `main` and `development`, so proposed changes are
7: validated before merge.
8: 
9: ## Original Goal
10: 
11: - create automated pull-request test execution for the repository
12: - run the full test suite from `tests/` whenever a PR is opened or updated
13: - expose a pass/fail GitHub check that can be required to block merging until
14:   tests pass
15: 
16: ## Original Plan
17: 
18: 1. add a GitHub Actions workflow under `.github/workflows/`
19: 2. trigger it on `pull_request` for `main` and `development`
20: 3. set up the documented repository environment with `uv` and Python `3.14`
21: 4. install dependencies and the editable package
22: 5. run the automated tests from `tests/`
23: 6. update persistent documentation so future contributors know the CI behavior
24: 
25: ## Adjustments Made During Implementation
26: 
27: 1. the workflow was kept to a single `ubuntu-latest` job because the repository
28:    documents only one Python baseline: `3.14`
29: 2. the workflow uses `.python-version` through `actions/setup-python` so the CI
30:    runner stays aligned with the repository baseline without duplicating the
31:    version string in multiple places
32: 3. merge blocking is documented as a GitHub branch-protection or ruleset concern
33:    outside the workflow file itself; the workflow provides the `tests` status
34:    check that can be marked as required in the GitHub UI
35: 
36: ## Implementation Performed
37: 
38: The following workflow was added:
39: 
40: - `.github/workflows/pr-tests.yml`
41: 
42: Implemented behavior:
43: 
44: - runs on `pull_request` targeting:
45:   - `main`
46:   - `development`
47: - runs for pull-request lifecycle events:
48:   - `opened`
49:   - `reopened`
50:   - `synchronize`
51: - checks out the repository
52: - sets up Python from `.python-version`
53: - installs `uv`
54: - synchronizes the repository environment with:
55:   - `uv sync --group codegen --group testing`
56: - installs the editable project package with:
57:   - `uv pip install -e .`
58: - runs the full automated test suite from `tests/` with:
59:   - `uv run pytest tests`
60: 
61: The workflow job is named `tests` so GitHub can expose a stable pull-request
62: check name for repository rules.
63: 
64: ## Verification
65: 
66: Implementation verification for issue `#25` is based on the same command the
67: workflow executes:
68: 
69: ```bash
70: uv run pytest tests
71: ```
72: 
73: Expected GitHub verification after the workflow file is pushed:
74: 
75: 1. open or update a pull request targeting `main` or `development`
76: 2. confirm the `tests` workflow job appears in the PR checks
77: 3. confirm the check passes when the suite passes
78: 4. confirm the check fails when a test in `tests/` fails
79: 
80: ## Findings
81: 
82: ### Positive Results
83: 
84: - the repository now has a single documented CI entry point for pull-request
85:   test execution
86: - the workflow follows the same `uv`-based environment setup already documented
87:   for local development
88: - using `uv run pytest tests` keeps the CI scope aligned with the repository
89:   convention that all automated tests live under `tests/`
90: 
91: ### Operational Finding
92: 
93: - the workflow itself reports status back to pull requests, but merge blocking is
94:   enforced only after the repository owner marks the `tests` check as required
95:   through GitHub branch protection or rulesets
96: 
97: ## Known Limitations
98: 
99: - issue `#25` adds pull-request test automation only; it does not add release,
100:   push, lint, or matrix CI workflows
101: - merge blocking depends on GitHub repository settings and cannot be enforced by
102:   workflow YAML alone
103: 
104: ## Impact On Future Issues
105: 
106: - future test additions should remain under `tests/` so they are included by the
107:   CI entry point without extra workflow maintenance
108: - issue `#16` can build on this workflow if the repository later needs broader
109:   pipeline coverage beyond the current test suite
110: - issue `#17` can reference this workflow as part of the final documented
111:   contributor and regeneration workflow
112: 
113: ## Status
114: 
115: - Status: implemented

1: # CVN Source Package Auxiliary Artifacts
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This document explains the auxiliary families that accompany the core CVN XML
6: package and that are required to understand the full official source bundle.
7: 
8: The project documentation already covered the core functional and structural
9: files:
10: 
11: - `SpecificationManual.xml`
12: - `CVNTreeModel.xml`
13: - `CVN.xsd`
14: - `Common.xsd`
15: - `AuxTable.xsd`
16: - `ISOUtilities.xsd`
17: 
18: This document covers the side packages that were present in the canonical source
19: bundle but had not yet been documented in comparable detail:
20: 
21: - the `Entity` family
22: - the `ReferenceTables` and `Subtypes` family
23: - the `Thesaurus` family
24: 
25: These families are not optional background material. They carry controlled
26: catalogs, multilingual labels, and supporting schemas that are referenced by
27: the main CVN manual and are relevant to later semantic mapping work.
28: 
29: ## Position Inside The Canonical Package
30: 
31: The canonical source bundle now needs to be read as two related zones.
32: 
33: ### Core CVN Specification Zone
34: 
35: - `Manual/Manual de Especificaciones Técnicas v1.4.3_v2.1.pdf`
36: - `Manual/TreeModel_v1.0 20090331 v1.0.pdf`
37: - `XML/SpecificationManual.xml`
38: - `XML/CVNTreeModel.xml`
39: - `XSD/CVN.xsd`
40: - `XSD/Common.xsd`
41: - `XSD/AuxTable.xsd`
42: - `XSD/ISOUtilities.xsd`
43: - `XSD/SpecificationManual.xsd`
44: - `XSD/CVNTreeModel_v1.0.xsd`
45: 
46: ### Auxiliary Catalog And Supporting Zone
47: 
48: - `LeemeENTITY.txt`
49: - `XML/Entity.xml`
50: - `XSD/Entity_v1.4.xsd`
51: - `XSD/EntityUtilities_v1.4.xsd`
52: - `XSD/ISOUtilitiesENTITY.xsd`
53: - `XSD/CVNUtilities_v1.0.xsd`
54: - `Manual/Entidades_esquema_Entity_v1.4.xsd_2008-07-04 v1.0.pdf`
55: - `HTML/Entity_v1.4.html`
56: - `LeemeREFERENCETABLES.txt`
57: - `XML/ReferenceTables.xml`
58: - `XML/Subtype_Spa.xml`
59: - `XSD/ReferenceTables.xsd`
60: - `XSD/ISOUtilitiesREFERENCETABLES.xsd`
61: - `XSD/Subtypes.xsd`
62: - `Manual/ReferenceTables.pdf`
63: - `Manual/Subtypes_v1.1.pdf`
64: - `LeemeTHESAURUS.txt`
65: - `XML/Thesaurus.xml`
66: - `XML/Thesaurus_Eng.xml`
67: - `XML/Thesaurus_Spa.xml`
68: - `XSD/Thesaurus.xsd`
69: - `XSD/ISOUtilitiesTHESAURUS.xsd`
70: - `Manual/Tesauros 2008-01-23 v1.0.pdf`
71: - `HTML/Thesaurus.html`
72: 
73: ## Family 1 - Entity
74: 
75: ## What It Is
76: 
77: The `Entity` family defines the normalization model used by CVN to represent
78:  institutions, organizations, centers, departments, and other institutional
79:  actors.
80: 
81: It is not the main CVN curriculum schema. It is a companion entity catalog and
82: entity schema that the functional manual references through expressions such as
83: `ENTITY@Entity.xsd`.
84: 
85: In practice, it provides:
86: 
87: - a normalized entity registry in XML form
88: - a dedicated XSD to validate that registry
89: - auxiliary controlled codes for entity nature, function, and type
90: - region, province, and street type helpers reused in entity addresses
91: 
92: ## Files And Roles
93: 
94: ### `LeemeENTITY.txt`
95: 
96: Quick orientation file for the family.
97: 
98: What it tells us:
99: 
100: - the family is intended for entity codification in CVN
101: - `Entity_v1.4.xsd` is described as a more advanced schema than the older
102:   `Entity.xsd`
103: - the exported entities remain the same, but the schema exposes more detail
104: - the package includes manual, XML, XSD, and HTML views
105: 
106: ### `Manual/Entidades_esquema_Entity_v1.4.xsd_2008-07-04 v1.0.pdf`
107: 
108: Human-readable explanation of `Entity_v1.4.xsd`.
109: 
110: Its value is high because it states the intended semantics of fields that would
111: otherwise be visible only as schema mechanics.
112: 
113: Important semantic points captured in the PDF:
114: 
115: - an entity is an institution, corporation, or company assigned a unique
116:   identifier for terminology normalization
117: - each normalized entity is represented by one `item`
118: - `ItemId` is the unique entity identifier and the document states that EAN-128
119:   is intended for the coding strategy
120: - entity function may be hierarchical through one or more `ItemAncestorId`
121: - `Delegate` means logical deactivation and redirection to a new `ItemId`
122: 
123: ### `XSD/Entity_v1.4.xsd`
124: 
125: Main schema of the family.
126: 
127: Root element:
128: 
129: - `Entity`
130: 
131: Top-level structure:
132: 
133: - repeated `item`
134: - root attribute `version`
135: 
136: Each `item` can contain:
137: 
138: - `ItemId`
139: - `Nature`
140: - repeated `Function`
141: - `Type`
142: - `ItemAddress`
143: - repeated `ItemDescription`
144: - `Synonym`
145: - `URL`
146: - repeated `ItemNote`
147: - `Delegate`
148: 
149: The schema therefore models a single entity as a registry record with identity,
150: classification, address, multilingual naming, aliases, optional notes, and a
151: logical-redirection mechanism.
152: 
153: ### `XSD/EntityUtilities_v1.4.xsd`
154: 
155: Controlled-value helper schema for the entity family.
156: 
157: It defines:
158: 
159: - `CVN_ENTITY_NATURE`
160:   - `000` public
161:   - `010` private
162:   - `020` mixed
163: - `CVN_ENTITY_FUNCTION`
164:   - `000` research
165:   - `010` work
166:   - `020` teaching
167:   - `030` health
168: - `CVN_ENTITY_TYPE`
169:   - entity categories such as university, institute, foundation, public
170:     research body, enterprise, health institution, technology center, and
171:     others
172: 
173: This file is especially important because the values used in the entity package
174: line up with values referenced from the main CVN package through
175: `CVN_ENTITY_TYPE`.
176: 
177: ### `XSD/ISOUtilitiesENTITY.xsd`
178: 
179: Entity-family copy of ISO controlled values.
180: 
181: The practical role observed in the package is to provide:
182: 
183: - `ISO_639` for multilingual text attributes
184: - `ISO_3166` and related country-code support
185: 
186: The existence of a family-specific ISO utility file means the official source
187: bundle duplicated ISO support instead of centralizing it in one shared artifact.
188: 
189: ### `XSD/CVNUtilities_v1.0.xsd`
190: 
191: Shared CVN helper catalog reused by the entity package.
192: 
193: The most relevant role visible in this context is that it provides CVN-level
194: codes such as:
195: 
196: - `CVN_Region`
197: - `CVN_Province`
198: - `CVN_STREET_TYPE`
199: 
200: This means entity addresses are not free-form only. They can combine text with
201: CVN-normalized geopolitical and street-type codes.
202: 
203: ### `XML/Entity.xml`
204: 
205: XML instance containing the actual entity catalog.
206: 
207: Observed characteristics from the instance:
208: 
209: - root `Entity` with namespace `http://cv.normalizado.org/entity`
210: - repeated `item` records using `xmlns=""` for local elements
211: - multilingual descriptions through `ItemDescription lang="spa"` and, in the
212:   full file, potentially other languages
213: - many institutional acronyms such as `CAEND`, `CAR`, `CCHS`, `CINN`, `CIN2`
214: - address blocks containing country code, city, street, and optional region or
215:   province
216: 
217: The file behaves as a normalized institutional authority file rather than a
218: small support list.
219: 
220: Observed scale of the catalog in the preserved XML:
221: 
222: - `16,459` entity records
223: - language-tagged descriptions observed in:
224:   - `spa`
225:   - `cat`
226:   - `eng`
227:   - `eus`
228:   - `glg`
229: - observed distribution of entity `Type` values includes strong presence of:
230:   - `080` entity enterprise
231:   - `100` health institutions
232:   - `020` university centers and assimilated structures
233:   - `OTHERS`
234: - observed function-code distribution includes all four declared function
235:   classes:
236:   - `000` research
237:   - `010` work
238:   - `020` teaching
239:   - `030` health
240: 
241: ### Real XML Usage Patterns
242: 
243: The preserved XML does not use all schema flexibilities equally.
244: 
245: Observed recurrent patterns:
246: 
247: - all records have `ItemId`
248: - all records have exactly one `ItemAddress`
249: - all records have exactly one `Synonym` element, but in most cases that element
250:   is empty and behaves like a materialized optional container
251: - `Function`, `Type`, `Nature`, and `URL` appear together in a large enriched
252:   subset of records, but are absent in many minimal reference records
253: - `Function` is never repeated in practice even though the XSD allows repeated
254:   occurrences
255: - `ItemAncestorId` is effectively singular in practice, even though the XSD
256:   allows repetition
257: - `ItemNote` is at most one per entity in the observed data, despite the schema
258:   allowing repetition
259: - multilingual `ItemDescription` follows a real-world pattern of either:
260:   - only `spa`
261:   - or a five-language bundle with `spa`, `cat`, `eng`, `eus`, `glg`
262: 
263: Observed practical consequences:
264: 
265: - the XML contains both minimal and enriched record profiles
266: - empty optional nodes often mean “no data” rather than intentional semantic
267:   content
268: - a semantic importer should normalize empty present nodes to null-like values
269: 
270: ### Address And Identifier Particularities
271: 
272: Observed data behavior makes the following points explicit.
273: 
274: - `CountryCode` is consistently present and overwhelmingly fixed to Spain in the
275:   observed data
276: - `Region` and `Province` often exist as empty nodes rather than being omitted
277: - `PostalCode` appears only in a structured subset of addresses
278: - `ItemNote` is heavily used as a vehicle for support-side identifiers and, in
279:   practice, behaves more like an external identifier attachment than like a free
280:   narrative note
281: - some URLs are placeholders and not genuine institutional URLs, so semantic
282:   validation of URL quality must happen outside the XSD layer
283: 
284: ### Implications For Semantic Modeling
285: 
286: The observed XML suggests at least two logical record profiles:
287: 
288: - minimal registry entries used as lightweight references
289: - enriched registry entries with classification, address detail, URL, and
290:   additional support metadata
291: 
292: This matters for later issues because it suggests that a future domain layer may
293: need:
294: 
295: - a normalized entity reference concept
296: - optional enrichment facets
297: - explicit relationship handling for `Delegate` and ancestor links
298: 
299: ### `HTML/Entity_v1.4.html`
300: 
301: HTML rendering of the schema.
302: 
303: This is useful as a navigation aid but does not add normative content beyond the
304: PDF and XSD.
305: 
306: ## Internal Model Of An Entity Record
307: 
308: An entity record combines the following semantic layers.
309: 
310: ### Identity Layer
311: 
312: - `ItemId`
313: 
314: ### Classification Layer
315: 
316: - `Nature`
317: - one or more `Function`
318: - `Type`

1: # CVN Annex Table Coverage
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This document explains how the auxiliary tables listed in Annex I of the CVN
6: technical manual are represented across the official source bundle shipped in the
7: repository.
8: 
9: The goal is practical:
10: 
11: - identify which tables are already machine-readable inside the package
12: - distinguish core-package tables from side-package catalogs
13: - make explicit which tables remain unresolved or only visible in the manual
14: 
15: This avoids treating Annex I as a monolithic block and gives later pipeline
16: stages a clearer source-of-truth policy.
17: 
18: ## Scope
19: 
20: The analysis is based on:
21: 
22: - `Manual de Especificaciones Técnicas v1.4.3_v2.1.pdf`, Annex I from page 308
23: - `XSD/AuxTable.xsd`
24: - `XSD/ISOUtilities.xsd`
25: - `XML/ReferenceTables.xml`
26: - `XML/Entity.xml`
27: - `XML/Thesaurus*.xml`
28: - supporting family-specific XSDs and manuals
29: 
30: This is a coverage map, not an exhaustive item-by-item dump of every enum value.
31: 
32: ## Coverage Model
33: 
34: Annex tables fall into three practical categories.
35: 
36: ### Category 1 - Directly Represented In Core XSD Artifacts
37: 
38: These tables are encoded directly in the core schemas used by the main CVN
39: document model.
40: 
41: Typical examples:
42: 
43: - `ISO_3166`
44: - `ISO_639`
45: - CVN helper types from `AuxTable.xsd`
46: 
47: Examples of directly encoded CVN controlled sets in `AuxTable.xsd`:
48: 
49: - `CVN_SOURCE_B`
50: - `CVN_LANGUAGE_B`
51: - `CVN_ACCESS_A`
52: - `CVN_ACTIVITY_A`
53: - `CVN_ACTIVITY_B`
54: - `CVN_CATEGORY_A`
55: - `CVN_DEDICATION_A`
56: - `CVN_DURATION_A`
57: - `CVN_ENTITY_TYPE`
58: - `CVN_EVALUATION_A`
59: - `CVN_EVENT_A`
60: - `CVN_EVENT_B`
61: - `CVN_EVENT_C`
62: - `CVN_FORMATION_A`
63: - `CVN_KNOW_A`
64: - `CVN_MANAGEMENT_A`
65: - `CVN_MANAGEMENT_TYPE_A`
66: - `CVN_PARTICIPATION_*`
67: - `CVN_PRIZE_A`
68: - `CVN_PROGRAMME_*`
69: - `CVN_PROJECT_*`
70: - `CVN_PUBLICATION_A`
71: - `CVN_QUALIFICATION_*`
72: - `CVN_SEX_A`
73: - `CVN_SITUATION_A`
74: - `CVN_STAY_*`
75: - `CVN_SUBJECT_A`
76: - `CVN_SUMMONS_*`
77: - `CVN_SUPPORT_*`
78: - `CVN_TEACHING_*`
79: - `CVN_THEMATIC_*`
80: - `CVN_TIME_A`
81: - `CVN_TITLE_*`
82: 
83: ### Why This Matters
84: 
85: These tables are the safest candidates for direct structural extraction and for
86: future semantic treatment as package-native controlled values.
87: 
88: They are the least ambiguous part of Annex I from an automation perspective.
89: 
90: ## Category 2 - Represented In Side Packages
91: 
92: These tables are not necessarily encoded directly inside the core CVN schema, but
93: they are still represented in machine-readable auxiliary packages bundled with
94: the source package.
95: 
96: ### 2.1 ReferenceTables And Subtypes
97: 
98: The strongest machine-readable representation of Annex I is the
99: `ReferenceTables` family.
100: 
101: `XML/ReferenceTables.xml` contains 73 tables, including:
102: 
103: - `CVN_SEX_A`
104: - `CVN_TITLE_B`
105: - `CVN_LANGUAGE_B`
106: - `CVN_PUBLICATION_A`
107: - `CVN_SUMMONS_A`
108: - `CVN_SUMMONS_B`
109: - `CVN_ENTITY_TYPE`
110: - `CVN_SOURCE_A`
111: - `CVN_SOURCE_B`
112: - `CVN_SOURCE_C`
113: - `CVN_SOURCE_DATO`
114: - `CVN_REGION`
115: - `CVN_PROVINCE`
116: - `UNESCO_CODES`
117: - `ISO_3166`
118: - `ISO_639`
119: 
120: This means Annex I is not only in the PDF. A substantial part of it is already
121: serialized in XML and backed by `ReferenceTables.xsd`.
122: 
123: For the specific case of `UNESCO_CODES`, the repository now also includes a
124: standalone extracted representation derived from `ReferenceTables.xml`:
125: 
126: - `docs/CvnXML_v1.4.3_2.1_17012025/XML/UNESCO_CODES.xml`
127: - `docs/CvnXML_v1.4.3_2.1_17012025/XSD/UNESCOCodes.xsd`
128: 
129: These files are repository-derived extraction artifacts, created to isolate the
130: UNESCO subject classification as its own reusable XML/XSD pair while preserving
131: all item-level fields present in the packaged source table.
132: 
133: `Subtype_Spa.xml` is not a replacement for Annex I, but a derived codification
134: layer used when a table value must be projected into `Subtype` fields in the
135: operational CVN XML.
136: 
137: ### 2.2 Entity Family
138: 
139: The manual repeatedly references `ENTITY@Entity.xsd` for entity-valued fields.
140: 
141: In the repository, the actual backing family is:
142: 
143: - `XSD/Entity_v1.4.xsd`
144: - `XML/Entity.xml`
145: - helper schemas `EntityUtilities_v1.4.xsd`, `ISOUtilitiesENTITY.xsd`, and
146:   `CVNUtilities_v1.0.xsd`
147: 
148: This family does not correspond to a simple enum table. It is a normalized
149: registry of institutions and organizations.
150: 
151: Therefore, whenever Annex I references entity-based values, the correct reading
152: is usually:
153: 
154: - not a closed enum
155: - but a catalog-backed external reference with structured metadata
156: 
157: ### 2.3 Thesaurus Family
158: 
159: The manual references `THESAURUS@thesaurus.xsd` for keyword-like controlled
160: fields.
161: 
162: In the repository, the backing family is:
163: 
164: - `XSD/Thesaurus.xsd`
165: - `XML/Thesaurus.xml`
166: - `XML/Thesaurus_Eng.xml`
167: - `XML/Thesaurus_Spa.xml`
168: 
169: This family is not a flat code list. It is a hierarchical multilingual thesaurus
170: for subject and keyword codification.
171: 
172: ### Why Category 2 Matters
173: 
174: These tables are machine-readable, but they should not all be treated the same
175: way as inline core enums.
176: 
177: They split into several semantic kinds:
178: 
179: - strict auxiliary tables
180: - hierarchical tables
181: - entity catalogs
182: - subtype projection maps
183: - multilingual thesauri
184: 
185: Future semantic generation should therefore preserve this distinction.
186: 
187: ## Category 3 - Manual-Only Or Unresolved From The Package Alone
188: 
189: Some Annex references cannot be traced cleanly to a machine-readable backing
190: artifact in the current package, or remain ambiguous enough that the package
191: alone does not provide a confident closed-world interpretation.
192: 
193: ### Confirmed Example: `CVN_AGENCY_C`
194: 
195: The table name `CVN_AGENCY_C` appears referenced in the manual material, but no
196: clear matching table was found in `ReferenceTables.xml`.
197: 
198: This makes it a known unresolved case from the package alone.
199: 
200: ### Other Practical Cases
201: 
202: Any Annex table that is only visible in the manual PDF and cannot be traced to:
203: 
204: - `AuxTable.xsd`
205: - `ReferenceTables.xml`
206: - `Entity.xml`
207: - `Thesaurus.xml`
208: 
209: should remain in this category until proven otherwise.
210: 
211: ### Why Category 3 Matters
212: 
213: These tables should not be turned into strict generated enums or treated as fully
214: resolved references without an explicit policy.
215: 
216: For the current project stage, the safest treatment is:
217: 
218: - document the gap explicitly
219: - keep the representation open or manually reviewed
220: - defer strict semantic closure to later issues only if stronger evidence is
221:   obtained
222: 
223: ## Practical Mapping Rules For The Project
224: 
225: The following source-of-truth policy is the most useful one for the repository.
226: 
227: ### Rule 1 - Prefer Core XSD Tables When They Exist
228: 
229: If a table is encoded directly in `AuxTable.xsd` or `ISOUtilities.xsd`, it
230: belongs to the core structural layer.
231: 
232: ### Rule 2 - Prefer `ReferenceTables.xml` For Annex-I Table Materialization
233: 
234: If a table is listed in Annex I and also present in `ReferenceTables.xml`, then
235: `ReferenceTables.xml` is the best machine-readable source of the table's items,
236: labels, hierarchy, and delegation behavior.
237: 
238: ### Rule 3 - Treat `Entity` As A Registry, Not As A Flat Enum
239: 
240: When the manual references `ENTITY@Entity.xsd`, the right semantic model is a
241: structured external registry of institutions.
242: 
243: ### Rule 4 - Treat `Thesaurus` As A Hierarchical Vocabulary, Not As A Flat Enum
244: 
245: When the manual references `THESAURUS@thesaurus.xsd`, the right semantic model is
246: a multilingual hierarchical subject vocabulary.
247: 
248: ### Rule 5 - Record Unresolved Tables Explicitly
249: 
250: If a table name cannot be traced to a concrete XML/XSD representation, it must be
251: kept as a documented unresolved case.
252: 
253: ## Tables With Especially High Importance For Later Issues
254: 
255: The following categories are especially relevant for issue `#14` and issue `#15`.
256: 
257: ### High Priority - Controlled Tables With Strong Semantic Impact
258: 
259: - `CVN_ENTITY_TYPE`
260: - `CVN_PUBLICATION_A`
261: - `CVN_PARTICIPATION_*`
262: - `CVN_PROJECT_*`
263: - `CVN_TITLE_*`
264: - `CVN_SUMMONS_*`
265: - `CVN_SOURCE_*`
266: 
267: ### High Priority - Large Or Hierarchical Vocabularies
268: 
269: - `UNESCO_CODES`
270: - `CVN_REGION`
271: - `CVN_PROVINCE`
272: - `Thesaurus`
273: 
274: ### High Priority - Externalized Structured Catalogs
275: 
276: - `Entity`
277: - `ReferenceTables`
278: - `Subtype`
279: 
280: ## Particularities To Keep In Mind
281: 
282: ### Annex I Is Split Across Several Technical Sources
283: 
284: The auxiliary tables in the manual do not live in one single technical file.
285: 
286: They are distributed across:
287: 
288: - core helper XSDs
289: - `ReferenceTables`
290: - `Entity`
291: - `Thesaurus`
292: 
293: ### The Official Package Preserves Historical Drift
294: 
295: There are visible mismatches in:
296: 
297: - filenames mentioned by `Leeme` files versus actual repository filenames
298: - schema versions between XSD, XML, and PDF companions
299: - relative `schemaLocation` values versus repository layout
300: 
301: This means coverage should be documented semantically, not inferred only from
302: literal path names.
303: 
304: ### Not Every Manual Reference Implies A Closed Enum
305: 
306: Some references point to:
307: 
308: - enumerations
309: - hierarchical tables
310: - subtype maps
311: - registries
312: - thesauri
313: 
314: Later semantic work should keep these categories distinct.
315: 
316: ## Summary
317: 
318: Annex I is only partially embedded in the core XSD layer.
319: 
320: The actual technical representation of Annex tables across the package is:

<content>
1: # CVN Serialization Patterns Reference
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This document explains the recurring serialization patterns used by CVN for
6: controlled tables, external catalogs, and auxiliary references.
7: 
8: The main point is that the semantic meaning of a table is not captured only by
9: its name. It is also encoded in the technical projection metadata used by the
10: source package, especially in `ReferenceTables.xml`.
11: 
12: The most useful fields for identifying the pattern are:
13: 
14: - `XMLDataType`
15: - `XMLProperty`
16: - `XMLIndicator`
17: 
18: This document is meant to be a practical bridge between:
19: 
20: - the functional manual
21: - the auxiliary tables
22: - the technical XML serialization
23: - the future semantic mapping policy in issue `#14`
24: 
25: ## Pattern 1 - `Filter/Value`
26: 
27: ## Shape
28: 
29: - `XMLDataType`: usually `CVN_Value_Filter@AuxTable.xsd`
30: - `XMLProperty`: `Filter`
31: - `XMLIndicator`: `Value`
32: 
33: ## Meaning
34: 
35: This is the most common serialization pattern for compact controlled tables.
36: 
37: It means the selected table value is carried as a generic filtered value in the
38: CVN XML, but the domain meaning must still come from the referenced table.
39: 
40: ## Typical Examples
41: 
42: - `CVN_SUBJECT_A`
43: - `CVN_STAY_A`
44: - `CVN_STAY_B`
45: - `CVN_ACTIVITY_A`
46: - `CVN_ACTIVITY_D`
47: - `CVN_MANAGEMENT_A`
48: - `CVN_MANAGEMENT_TYPE_A`
49: - `CVN_SUMMONS_A`
50: - `CVN_SUMMONS_B`
51: - `CVN_PRIZE_A`
52: - `CVN_THEMATIC_A`
53: - `CVN_THEMATIC_B`
54: - `CVN_ACCESS_A`
55: - `CVN_EVALUATION_A`
56: - many more compact CVN tables
57: 
58: ## Why It Matters
59: 
60: Two tables using `Filter/Value` are not necessarily semantically close.
61: 
62: For example:
63: 
64: - `CVN_SUBJECT_A` classifies subject type
65: - `CVN_STAY_A` classifies objective of a stay
66: - `CVN_ACCESS_A` classifies access procedure
67: 
68: They share a technical projection, not a shared domain concept.
69: 
70: ## Pattern 2 - `Quality/Measure`
71: 
72: ## Shape
73: 
74: - `XMLProperty`: `Quality`
75: - `XMLIndicator`: `Measure`
76: 
77: ## Meaning
78: 
79: This pattern is used for normalized measures, scales, and evaluative levels.
80: 
81: ## Typical Examples
82: 
83: - `CVN_LANGUAGE_B`
84: - `CVN_QUALIFICATION_B`
85: 
86: ## Why It Matters
87: 
88: These tables are usually better interpreted as scales or ratings than as generic
89: categories.
90: 
91: They are among the safest candidates for strict enums in the semantic layer.
92: 
93: ## Pattern 3 - `Scope/Type`
94: 
95: ## Shape
96: 
97: - `XMLProperty`: `Scope`
98: - `XMLIndicator`: `Type`
99: 
100: ## Meaning
101: 
102: This pattern classifies geographical or institutional scope.
103: 
104: ## Typical Examples
105: 
106: - `CVN_SCOPE_A`
107: - `CVN_SCOPE_B`
108: 
109: ## Why It Matters
110: 
111: Scope tables should usually become shared reusable domain concepts because they
112: are reused across many unrelated curriculum sections.
113: 
114: Also, `CVN_SCOPE_A` and `CVN_SCOPE_B` should not be merged automatically.
115: 
116: ## Pattern 4 - `ExternalPK/Type`
117: 
118: ## Shape
119: 
120: - `XMLProperty`: `ExternalPK`
121: - `XMLIndicator`: `Type`
122: 
123: ## Meaning
124: 
125: This pattern classifies the type of external identifier, not the identifier
126: value itself.
127: 
128: ## Typical Examples
129: 
130: - `CVN_SOURCE_B`
131: - `CVN_SOURCE_C`
132: 
133: ## Why It Matters
134: 
135: The domain layer should preserve the distinction between:
136: 
137: - identifier type
138: - identifier value
139: 
140: This is especially important for publication identifiers and author identifiers.
141: 
142: ## Pattern 5 - `Entity/Type`
143: 
144: ## Shape
145: 
146: - `XMLProperty`: `Entity`
147: - `XMLIndicator`: `Type`
148: 
149: ## Meaning
150: 
151: This pattern classifies the type of institution referenced by a CVN field.
152: 
153: ## Typical Example
154: 
155: - `CVN_ENTITY_TYPE`
156: 
157: ## Why It Matters
158: 
159: This is not the same as the `Entity` family itself.
160: 
161: - `CVN_ENTITY_TYPE` is a small type table
162: - `Entity.xml` is a large normalized institution registry
163: 
164: Both concepts must stay distinct in later semantic modeling.
165: 
166: ## Pattern 6 - `Dedication`
167: 
168: ## Shape
169: 
170: - `XMLDataType`: `CVN_DedicationType@AuxTable.xsd`
171: - `XMLProperty`: `Dedication`
172: - no `XMLIndicator`
173: 
174: ## Meaning
175: 
176: This is a specialized dedicated pattern for work dedication regime.
177: 
178: ## Typical Example
179: 
180: - `CVN_DEDICATION_A`
181: 
182: ## Why It Matters
183: 
184: This table is small, stable, and heavily reused across different sections. It is
185: an excellent candidate for a shared domain enum.
186: 
187: ## Pattern 7 - `PhysicalDimension/Type`
188: 
189: ## Shape
190: 
191: - `XMLProperty`: `PhysicalDimension`
192: - `XMLIndicator`: `Type`
193: 
194: ## Meaning
195: 
196: This pattern encodes the unit or dimension in which a quantity is expressed.
197: 
198: ## Typical Example
199: 
200: - `CVN_TIME_A`
201: 
202: ## Why It Matters
203: 
204: This is not a thematic classification. It determines the meaning of a numeric
205: value, such as whether teaching load is measured in hours or credits.
206: 
207: ## Pattern 8 - `Subject/Description`
208: 
209: ## Shape
210: 
211: - `XMLProperty`: `Subject`
212: - `XMLIndicator`: `Description`
213: 
214: ## Meaning
215: 
216: This pattern is used for subject hierarchies or thematic classifications.
217: 
218: ## Typical Example
219: 
220: - `UNESCO_CODES`
221: 
222: ## Why It Matters
223: 
224: This pattern points to a hierarchical thematic vocabulary rather than a flat enum.
225: 
226: It should normally be treated as a lookup-backed classification tree.
227: 
228: ## Pattern 9 - `Subtype@Subtypes.xsd`
229: 
230: ## Shape
231: 
232: - `XMLDataType`: `Subtype@Subtypes.xsd`
233: - `XMLProperty`: `Subtype`
234: - usually no `XMLIndicator`
235: 
236: ## Meaning
237: 
238: This is not a normal direct-value serialization.
239: 
240: The selected code is projected into the `Subtype` structure of the operational
241: CVN XML, potentially through one or two levels (`SubType1` / `SubType2`).
242: 
243: ## Typical Examples
244: 
245: - `CVN_FORMATION_A`
246: - `CVN_TEACHING_A`
247: - `CVN_KNOW_A`
248: - `CVN_PROJECT_A`
249: - `CVN_PUBLICATION_A`
250: - `CVN_SUPPORT_A`
251: - `CVN_SUPPORT_B`
252: - `CVN_EVENT_A`
253: - `CVN_EVENT_B`
254: - `CVN_EVENT_C`
255: - `CVN_ACTIVITY_B`
256: 
257: ## Why It Matters
258: 
259: This is one of the most important patterns in the package.
260: 
261: It means later semantic generation cannot treat all tables as direct enums.
262: 
263: Subtype-backed tables need:
264: 
265: - explicit traceability to subtype mapping rules
266: - awareness that the selected table code is not necessarily the final XML value
267:   written to the CVN item
268: 
269: ## Pattern 9b - `Identification/PersonalIdentification`
270: 
271: ## Shape
272: 
273: - `XMLProperty`: `Identification`
274: - `XMLIndicator`: `PersonalIdentification`
275: 
276: ## Meaning
277: 
278: This pattern is used for compact identity-classification fields attached to the
279: personal-identification area of CVN.
280: 
281: ## Typical Example
282: 
283: - `CVN_SEX_A`
284: 
285: ## Why It Matters
286: 
287: It is technically distinct from the more generic `Filter/Value` tables and
288: should be described with its own source-traceability pattern rather than being
289: silently folded into an unrelated generic class.
290: 
291: ## Pattern 10 - Catalog-Or-Registry Patterns
292: 
293: Some references do not behave like simple tables at all.
294: 
295: ## Entity Registry Pattern
296: 
297: Representative artifacts:
298: 
299: - `Entity.xml`
300: - `Entity_v1.4.xsd`
301: 
302: Meaning:
303: 
304: - large normalized institution catalog
305: - structured records, not plain enum members
306: 
307: ## Thesaurus Pattern
308: 
309: Representative artifacts:
310: 
311: - `Thesaurus.xml`
312: - `Thesaurus_Eng.xml`
313: - `Thesaurus_Spa.xml`
314: - `Thesaurus.xsd`
315: 
316: Meaning:
317: 
318: - hierarchical multilingual vocabulary
319: - external coded subject system, not a plain enum
320: 

(Showing lines 1-320 of 394. Use offset=321 to continue.)
</content>

2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This document explains how to trace a CVN field from the normalized manual layer
6: already implemented in the repository to the technical source artifact that

9:

11:

13: - avoid reopening the source package every time a field needs to be classified

18: 
19: The current repository implementation already exposes the key anchor needed for
20: this traceability work:
21: 
22: - `ManualCodeEntry.manual_reference_table`
23: 
24: This field is populated from `SpecificationManual.xml` during issue `#13`
25: normalization and is therefore the canonical bridge from a CVN field to its
26: controlled table or auxiliary catalog.
27: 
28: That means this document is intentionally additive.
29: 
30: It does not redefine the normalization layer. It explains how to interpret the
31: references already extracted by it.
32: 
33: ## Source Of Truth Layers
34: 
35: When a CVN field has a `manual_reference_table`, the repository should resolve it
36: through the following source-of-truth order.
37: 
38: ### Level 1 - `ReferenceTables.xml`
39: 
40: If the reference name exists as a table in `XML/ReferenceTables.xml`, that XML is
41: the primary machine-readable source for:
42: 
43: - codes
44: - multilingual labels
45: - hierarchy through `AntecesorCode`
46: - delegation through `Delegate`
47: - technical projection metadata such as:
48:   - `XMLDataType`
49:   - `XMLProperty`
50:   - `XMLIndicator`
51: 
52: ### Level 2 - Side Packages
53: 
54: If the manual reference points to an auxiliary family rather than a simple table,
55: the source of truth is the relevant side package.
56: 
57: #### Entity
58: 
59: Manual form:
60: 
61: - `ENTITY@Entity.xsd`
62: 
63: Backing artifacts:
64: 
65: - `XML/Entity.xml`
66: - `XSD/Entity_v1.4.xsd`
67: - helpers `EntityUtilities_v1.4.xsd`, `ISOUtilitiesENTITY.xsd`,
68:   `CVNUtilities_v1.0.xsd`
69: 
70: #### Thesaurus
71: 
72: Manual form:
73: 
74: - `THESAURUS@thesaurus.xsd`
75: 
76: Backing artifacts:
77: 
78: - `XML/Thesaurus.xml`
79: - `XML/Thesaurus_Eng.xml`
80: - `XML/Thesaurus_Spa.xml`
81: - `XSD/Thesaurus.xsd`
82: 
83: ### Level 3 - Manual-Only Or Unresolved Cases
84: 
85: If the manual reference does not resolve cleanly to `ReferenceTables.xml` or to
86: one of the side packages, it must remain documented as unresolved.
87: 
88: Known example:
89: 
90: - `CVN_AGENCY_C`
91: 
92: ## Resolution Procedure
93: 
94: For any normalized field, use this procedure.
95: 
96: 1. read `ManualCodeEntry.code`
97: 2. read `ManualCodeEntry.manual_reference_table`
98: 3. resolve the reference according to the rules below
99: 4. identify the serialization pattern
100: 5. classify the field as one of these semantic kinds:
101:    - compact enum-like table
102:    - hierarchical codelist
103:    - large registry or managed catalog
104:    - side-package external catalog
105:    - manual-only unresolved reference
106:    - technically present but functionally under-traced table
107: 
108: ## Resolution Rules
109: 
110: ### Rule 1 - Exact Match In `ReferenceTables.xml`
111: 
112: If the manual reference table name exists in `ReferenceTables.xml`, resolve it to:
113: 
114: - table metadata in `ReferenceTables.xml`
115: - the corresponding `ReferenceTables.xsd` structure
116: - subtype support if `XMLDataType` is `Subtype@Subtypes.xsd`
117: 
118: Examples:
119: 
120: - `CVN_SEX_A`
121: - `CVN_TITLE_B`
122: - `CVN_PROJECT_A`
123: - `CVN_LANGUAGE_B`
124: - `UNESCO_CODES`
125: 
126: ### Rule 2 - Exact Side-Package Reference
127: 
128: If the manual reference is an explicit auxiliary-package reference string, use
129: the side package instead of looking for a same-named table in `ReferenceTables`.
130: 
131: Examples:
132: 
133: - `ENTITY@Entity.xsd`
134: - `THESAURUS@thesaurus.xsd`
135: 
136: ### Rule 3 - Unresolved Manual Reference
137: 
138: If the manual uses a reference table name that has no matching `ReferenceTables`
139: table and no side-package backing, document it as unresolved.
140: 
141: Example:
142: 
143: - `CVN_AGENCY_C`
144: 
145: ### Rule 4 - Technically Present But Functionally Under-Traced Table
146: 
147: If a table exists in `ReferenceTables.xml` but the manual does not appear to use
148: it, keep it documented but lower its priority for semantic generation.
149: 
150: Examples:
151: 
152: - `CVN_INTERVENTION_A`
153: - `CVN_PRUEBA`
154: 
155: ## Serialization Pattern Map
156: 
157: The following pattern names are the ones that matter most for repository work.
158: 
159: ### `Filter/Value`
160: 
161: Meaning:
162: 
163: - compact direct controlled value carried as a generic filtered value
164: 
165: Examples:
166: 
167: - `CVN_SUBJECT_A`
168: - `CVN_STAY_A`
169: - `CVN_STAY_B`
170: - `CVN_ACTIVITY_A`
171: - `CVN_SUMMONS_B`
172: 
173: ### `Quality/Measure`
174: 
175: Meaning:
176: 
177: - normalized level or result scale
178: 
179: Examples:
180: 
181: - `CVN_LANGUAGE_B`
182: - `CVN_QUALIFICATION_B`
183: 
184: ### `Scope/Type`
185: 
186: Meaning:
187: 
188: - geographical or institutional scope type
189: 
190: Examples:
191: 
192: - `CVN_SCOPE_A`
193: - `CVN_SCOPE_B`
194: 
195: ### `ExternalPK/Type`
196: 
197: Meaning:
198: 
199: - type of external identifier
200: 
201: Examples:
202: 
203: - `CVN_SOURCE_B`
204: - `CVN_SOURCE_C`
205: 
206: ### `Entity/Type`
207: 
208: Meaning:
209: 
210: - compact type of institution
211: 
212: Example:
213: 
214: - `CVN_ENTITY_TYPE`
215: 
216: ### `Dedication`
217: 
218: Meaning:
219: 
220: - dedication regime without a generic indicator node
221: 
222: Example:
223: 
224: - `CVN_DEDICATION_A`
225: 
226: ### `PhysicalDimension/Type`
227: 
228: Meaning:
229: 
230: - dimension of quantitative measurement
231: 
232: Example:
233: 
234: - `CVN_TIME_A`
235: 
236: ### `Subject/Description`
237: 
238: Meaning:
239: 
240: - hierarchical subject classification
241: 
242: Example:
243: 
244: - `UNESCO_CODES`
245: 
246: ### `Subtype@Subtypes.xsd`
247: 
248: Meaning:
249: 
250: - selected value is projected into the `Subtype` structure instead of being used
251:   as a plain direct controlled value
252: 
253: Examples:

1: # Known Limitations
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This document records known limitations of the current pipeline so later issues
6: do not need to rediscover them.
7: 
8: ## Structural Binding Limitations
9: 
10: ### `xs:choice` Is Not Enforced As Mutual Exclusivity
11: 
12: - Affected areas include:
13:   - `FlexibleDatesType`
14:   - `OfficialIdType`
15:   - `EntityTypeType`
16:   - `EntityNameType`
17: - Impact:
18:   - generated Pydantic models may accept states that are invalid with respect to
19:     the source XSD
20: - Expected follow-up:
21:   - issue `#14` should define policy
22:   - issue `#15` should restore domain-facing semantics
23: 
24: ### `minOccurs` Is Not Enforced For Generated Lists
25: 
26: - Generated list fields with `default_factory=list` do not enforce the minimum
27:   cardinality implied by the XSD
28: - Impact:
29:   - empty lists may be accepted in object construction even when the XSD
30:     expects at least one element
31: - Expected follow-up:
32:   - issue `#14` and issue `#15`
33: 
34: ### Some Attributes Are Typed As `object`
35: 
36: - Seen in parts of `specification_manual` and `tree_model`
37: - Impact:
38:   - validation is weaker than the XSD suggests
39:   - ergonomics are worse for downstream code
40: - Expected follow-up:
41:   - issue `#14` and issue `#15`
42: 
43: ### XML Helper Types Are Less Ergonomic Than Primitives
44: 
45: - Wrappers such as `CVN_duration`, `CVN_gYear`, and `CVN_gYearMonth` map to XML
46:   helper types such as `XmlDuration` and `XmlPeriod`
47: - Impact:
48:   - structural fidelity is preserved, but programmatic usage is more delicate
49: - Expected follow-up:
50:   - issue `#14` and issue `#15`
51: 
52: ## Generation Process Limitations
53: 
54: ### `tree_model` Needs A Target-Specific xsdata Override
55: 
56: - Default structural generation hit circular dependency problems
57: - Current workaround:
58:   - `--unnest-classes`
59: - Impact:
60:   - generation is reproducible, but not uniform across all three targets
61: - Expected follow-up:
62:   - keep documented through issue `#17`
63: 
64: ## Canonical Source Package Inconsistencies
65: 
66: ### `CVNTreeModel.xml` Diverges From `CVNTreeModel_v1.0.xsd`
67: 
68: - Confirmed discrepancy:
69:   - the XML includes `<Type>` inside `Indicator`
70:   - the XSD only declares `Value` and `Child` inside `Indicator`
71: - Confirmed scope of the discrepancy:
72:   - the canonical XML contains `438` `Indicator` nodes with
73:     `mo:name="Type"`, which is compatible with the documented tree-model
74:     structure
75:   - only `2` real child elements named `<Type>` were found in the canonical XML
76:   - those `2` unexpected child elements appear under:
77:     - `Indicator mo:name="Type" mo:code="060.030.070.220"`
78:     - `Indicator mo:name="Type" mo:code="060.030.070.230"`
79:   - both unexpected child elements contain the value:
80:     `CVN_QualityTypeType@AuxTable.xsd`
81: - Comparison with the tree-model documentation:
82:   - `TreeModel_v1.0 20090331 v1.0.pdf` defines `Indicator` children as only
83:     `Value` and `Child`
84:   - the document does not describe `<Type>` as an allowed child element of
85:     `Indicator`
86:   - this makes the two `<Type>` elements a source inconsistency, not a
87:     documented feature of the tree model
88: - Practical consequence:
89:   - the generated `tree_model` binding is correct with respect to the XSD, but
90:     cannot fully parse the canonical XML file
91: - Normalization consequence:
92:   - issue `#13` should treat `xml_path` as a structural path built from
93:     `CVNTreeModel`, `Node`, `CVNItem`, `Property`, and `Indicator`
94:   - the unexpected `<Type>` child elements should be recorded as explicit
95:     mismatches or special-case findings, not folded into the standard structural
96:     path model
97: - Parse status:
98:   - `SpecificationManual.xml`: parse OK
99:   - `CVNTreeModel.xml`: parse blocked by XML/XSD mismatch
100: - Expected follow-up:
101:   - issue `#13` must treat the tree-model XML as a source of truth for
102:     normalization even when the XSD does not describe it completely
103: 
104: ### Auxiliary Catalog Families Preserve Historical Packaging Drift
105: 
106: - affected families:
107:   - `Entity`
108:   - `ReferenceTables/Subtypes`
109:   - `Thesaurus`
110: - confirmed issues:
111:   - XML `schemaLocation` values assume colocated XSD files, while the preserved
112:     repository package stores XML and XSD in separate directories
113:   - several `Leeme*.txt` files mention filenames that do not exactly match the
114:     preserved repository filenames, such as `Subtypes.xml` instead of
115:     `Subtype_Spa.xml`, or lowercase thesaurus filenames that differ from the
116:     actual files
117:   - side families duplicate ISO helper schemas instead of using one fully shared
118:     physical artifact
119:   - `Subtypes` materials preserve version drift between PDF, XSD, and XML files
120: - impact:
121:   - package exploration and automated file resolution cannot rely on filenames or
122:     relative schema locations alone
123:   - tooling must resolve these families through repository-aware path mapping and
124:     documented semantic relationships
125: - expected follow-up:
126:   - issue `#14` should define semantic policy for side-package references
127:   - issue `#15` should decide which of these auxiliary artifacts become domain
128:     sources versus support registries
129: 
130: ### Some Annex-I Table References Remain Unresolved From The Package Alone
131: 
132: - confirmed example:
133:   - `CVN_AGENCY_C` appears referenced from the manual material but does not map
134:     cleanly to a matching table in `ReferenceTables.xml`
135: - impact:
136:   - not every table name from the manual can yet be promoted to a strict
137:     machine-resolved enum or closed catalog using the source package alone
138: - expected follow-up:
139:   - issue `#14` should define open versus closed treatment for unresolved tables
140:   - issue `#15` should preserve such cases as explicit external or manual-only
141:     references unless stronger evidence is introduced
142: 
143: ## Documentation Rule
144: 
145: Whenever a new limitation is discovered, add it here and reference the issue
146: expected to address it.
